note: Three CNS-directed NAGLU programs: intracerebral rAAV2/5-hNAGLU (phase 1/2), IV SBC-103 (stopped after phase 1/2), and ICV tralesinidase alfa (phase 1/2, BLA planned on CSF HS, phase 3 registered).
label: MPS IIIB (NAGLU replacement)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC 21139569). Vector in dogs was AAV5-NAGLU; the clinical product is rAAV2/5-hNAGLU, treated as the same product family but product_in_model kept false.
engagement.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
engagement.note: Intracerebral rAAV5-NAGLU in immunosuppressed MPS IIIB dogs produced brain NAGLU and cleared storage; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: In immunosuppressed dogs, vector was efficiently delivered throughout the brain, induced α-N-acetyl-glucosaminidase production, cleared stored compounds and storage lesions.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the dog study is the stated basis for the human trial (rAAV2/5-hNAGLU, a member).

engagement.magnitude_basis: brain/CSF NAGLU enzyme activity after intracerebral vector
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 28713035); 4 patients; registry ISRCTN19853672/NCT03300453 (no posted results).
engagement.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
engagement.note: Patients given intracerebral rAAV2/5-hNAGLU had NAGLU activity in lumbar CSF at 15-20% of unaffected children, as the dog predicted.
engagement.short: CSF NAGLU detected in all 4 children
engagement.quote: NAGLU activity was detected in lumbar CSF and was 15-20% of that in unaffected children.
engagement.reason: Transgene NAGLU expressed in patients' CNS
engagement.judgement: Paired: the trial reports CSF enzyme, the dog paper brain enzyme; direction matches, magnitude not comparable across compartments.

engagement.confidence_note: Meeting abstract (Mol Genet Metab 111(2):S92); only the title could be read, quoted verbatim.
engagement.note: IV SBC-103 reduced CNS heparan sulfate in Naglu-/- mice (meeting abstract); basis for IV dosing in children.
engagement.short: IV enzyme lowers mouse CNS HS
engagement.quote: Intravenous SBC-103, a recombinant human alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase reduces CNS heparan sulfate content in a mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIB mouse model.
engagement.judgement: Only the title of this WORLDSymposium abstract is readable; it is the sole public model source for IV SBC-103.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CNS (mouse brain) vs CSF (patient) total heparan sulfate
engagement.confidence_note: Patient side abstract-level (PubMed 30635159); model side is a title-only meeting abstract. Year 2018 = registry results posting of NCT02324049.
engagement.note: In children, IV SBC-103 up to 10 mg/kg barely moved CSF heparan sulfate (-4.7% at week 52) and early falls were not maintained.
engagement.short: CSF HS change small, not maintained
engagement.quote: Changes in heparan sulfate levels in CSF were small and were not maintained from earlier study time points
engagement.reason: CSF heparan sulfate barely moved in patients
engagement.judgement: Paired: the mouse abstract predicted CNS HS reduction from IV enzyme; patient CSF HS was the closest human readout and did not fall durably. A 2016 sponsor release of a 26% early fall was superseded by the peer-reviewed final results.

engagement.note: ICV NAGLU-IGF2 in adult Naglu-/- mice was taken up across the brain and cleared heparan sulfate.
engagement.short: ICV fusion enzyme clears mouse brain HS
engagement.quote: There was marked uptake of the administered enzyme in many parts of the brain, where it persisted with a half-life of approximately 10 d.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry; the mouse is the first system for tralesinidase alfa (BMN 250).

engagement.magnitude_basis: heparan sulfate clearance (mouse brain tissue vs patient CSF)
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9843052). NCT02754076 has no posted results.
engagement.note: ICV tralesinidase alfa 300 mg normalized CSF and plasma HS and HS-NRE in patients, as ICV dosing cleared mouse brain HS.
engagement.quote: In the Part 1 dose escalation (30, 100, and 300 mg) phase, a 300 mg dose of tralesinidase alfa was necessary to achieve normalization of HS and HS-NRE levels in the CSF and plasma.
engagement.reason: Patient CSF HS normalized at top dose
engagement.judgement: Paired: the trial paper cites the animal work but does not set the mouse numbers beside its own. Both systems needed the highest dose tested for full clearance.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 35717448). Start year is a proxy; the paper's own study dates were not read.
engagement.model: MPS IIIB dog, ICV tralesinidase alfa (20 months)
engagement.note: 20-month ICV tralesinidase alfa study in MPS IIIB dogs (run alongside the IND) near-normalized CSF and CNS heparan sulfate.
engagement.short: Dog CSF HS near-normal on ICV enzyme
engagement.quote: MPS IIIB dogs treated for up to 20 months had near-normal levels of HS and nonreducing ends of HS in cerebrospinal fluid and central nervous system (CNS) tissues.
engagement.judgement: Opening year 2016 is a proxy (trial start, April 2016); the dog data were published only in 2022.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CSF HS-NRE relative to normal range (near-normal in dogs, normalized in patients)
engagement.model: MPS IIIB dog, ICV tralesinidase alfa (20 months)
engagement.note: Dog CSF HS-NRE normalization, which the sponsor treats as predicting benefit, was reproduced in 19 of 22 patients.
engagement.short: Patient CSF HS-NRE normalized as in dogs
engagement.quote: Data in the dog model of MPS IIIB demonstrated that HS-NRE levels in the CSF and brain correlate with each other; the normalization of HS-NRE levels in the CSF predicts benefits.
engagement.reason: Same CSF readout normalized in patients
engagement.judgement: Not a retrodiction: the dog study ran before patient data; publication order (dog 2022, patients 2023) agrees. Kept comparison_stated false because the trial paper invokes the dog result without setting numbers side by side.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC 15537895); full text PMC6730192 not read.
engagement.note: Single intraputaminal AAV5-NaGlu in 6-week Naglu-/- mice gave brain-wide NaGlu activity above physiological levels; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: Mouse brain NaGlu after AAV, pre-clinic
engagement.quote: High NaGlu activity, far above physiological levels, was measured in the brain and persisted at 38 weeks of age.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the Paris group's mouse study chose AAV5 over AAV2 for the intracerebral route later used with rAAV2/5-hNAGLU; a separate system from the draft's dog track and from the mouse IV/ICV enzyme tracks.

engagement.magnitude_basis: brain (mouse) vs lumbar CSF (patient) NAGLU activity after intracerebral AAV
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; n=4; ISRCTN19853672/NCT03300453 have no posted results. Patient quote taken from the draft's verified Tardieu 2017 entry.
engagement.note: Children given intracerebral rAAV2/5-hNAGLU had CSF NAGLU at 15-20% of unaffected children, as the mouse brain expression predicted.
engagement.short: CSF NAGLU detected in all 4 children
engagement.quote: NAGLU activity was detected in lumbar CSF and was 15-20% of that in unaffected children.
engagement.reason: Transgene NAGLU expressed in patients' CNS
engagement.judgement: Paired: mouse brain enzyme vs patient CSF enzyme; direction matches, levels not comparable (mouse supraphysiological, patients below normal).

dose.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
dose.note: Dog work informed vector type and dose, but no human vector dose or exposure target was stated in the paper.
dose.quote: The suitability of the procedure for clinical application was further assessed in Hurler dogs, providing information on reproducibility, tolerance, appropriate vector type and dosage, and optimal age for treatment in a total number of 25 treated dogs.
dose.reason: No stated human dose or margin
dose.judgement: The dosage information came from Hurler (MPS I) dogs and gave no checkable human target, so no dose comparison.

dose.note: Mouse abstract gives no human exposure target; patient doses (0.3-10 mg/kg) came from clinical escalation.
dose.quote: Intravenous SBC-103, a recombinant human alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase reduces CNS heparan sulfate content in a mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIB mouse model.
dose.judgement: Title-only source; no dose statement checkable.

dose.note: Mouse showed only the highest ICV dose fully cleared storage; patients likewise needed the 300 mg maximum feasible dose, but no human target was stated.
dose.short: Top dose needed in both; no target
dose.quote: The substantial brain uptake of NAGLU attainable by this highest ICV dosage was required for nearly complete attenuation of disease-driven storage accumulations and neuropathology throughout the Naglu-/- mouse brain.
dose.judgement: A looser reading would score same (both systems needed their top dose), but the mouse paper states no human exposure or dose, so untested. Mouse first used 2014 (Kan); entry dated to the dose-ranging paper.

dose.model: Juvenile cynomolgus monkey ICV toxicology (tralesinidase alfa)
dose.note: Juvenile NHP ICV study supported the pediatric route and regimen; no NOAEL-to-human-dose margin appears in the public paper.
dose.quote: The data support the administration of TA by isovolumetric bolus ICV infusion to pediatric patients with MPS IIIB.
dose.judgement: The tolerability margin was presumably in the IND but is not in the abstract; scored untested/unpublished.

dose.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9426762, BioC) read. Opening year 2016 is a proxy (trial start April 2016), as on this track's engagement entry.
dose.note: 20-month ICV study in MPS IIIB dogs at 12 and 48 mg every other week; dose scaled to humans by brain mass.
dose.short: Dog dose scaled by brain mass
dose.quote: Therefore, one appropriate method to scale doses across species to estimate an efficacious dose for human patients is to correct for brain mass.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the dog track's dose cell; the dog study stated both an effective-dose estimate and a tolerability margin, published 2022.
dose.model: MPS IIIB dog, ICV tralesinidase alfa (20 months)

dose.magnitude_basis: dog-predicted effective clinical dose (300 mg weekly, CSF HS normalization) vs dose that normalized patient CSF HS (300 mg)
dose.confidence_note: Dog full text read; Muschol 2023 full text quote from the draft's verified engagement entry. NCT02754076 has no posted results (checked). Subject to rule question 3 on margins published after trial start.
dose.note: Dogs tolerated 48 mg (about 960 mg every other week human-equivalent), a stated margin over 300 mg weekly; patients reached CSF HS normalization at 300 mg.
dose.short: 300 mg normalized CSF HS, margin held
dose.quote: In the Part 1 dose escalation (30, 100, and 300 mg) phase, a 300 mg dose of tralesinidase alfa was necessary to achieve normalization of HS and HS-NRE levels in the CSF and plasma.
dose.reason: 300 mg reached HS target; margin held
dose.judgement: Dog paper states 48 mg 'provides a sufficient safety margin over the clinical dose (300 mg weekly)' and 300 mg 'should normalize HS'; patients reached that at 300 mg and were kept on it. Partial: drug-related CSF pleocytosis SAEs (counted in safety). Same rule question as dose 4 (cyno-icv-ta-tox): margin published 2022, after the 2016 trial start but before patient data (2023); if the adjudicator rules such margins inadmissible, this becomes untested.
dose.model: MPS IIIB dog, ICV tralesinidase alfa (20 months)

efficacy.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
efficacy.note: Dog and earlier mouse work predicted that brain NAGLU expression prevents neurodegeneration.
efficacy.quote: Studies in the mouse model showed that gene therapy providing the missing enzyme α-N-acetyl-glucosaminidase to brain cells prevents neurodegeneration and improves behavior.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: developmental quotient decline vs natural history
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; uncontrolled comparison with natural history.
efficacy.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
efficacy.note: All four children still declined (DQ -11 to -29) but less than natural history (-37.7); youngest near normal.
efficacy.quote: Compared with the natural history of mucopolysaccharidosis type III syndromes, neurocognitive progression was improved in all patients, with the youngest patient having function close to that in healthy children.
efficacy.judgement: Registered primary endpoint was safety; scored on the neurocognitive outcome, the only efficacy readout, so endpoint_role left null. Uncontrolled n=4 against historical natural history, so partial and low confidence.

patient_trials.quote: Milder disease progression in the youngest patient was found associated with low level and less differentiated circulating NAGLU-specific T cells, together with the lack of proinflammatory cytokines in the CSF.

efficacy.note: Mouse CNS HS reduction with IV SBC-103 implied CNS disease modification from systemic enzyme.
efficacy.quote: Intravenous SBC-103, a recombinant human alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase reduces CNS heparan sulfate content in a mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIB mouse model.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CNS benefit predicted vs none observed
efficacy.note: No clinically meaningful neurocognitive improvement at 5-10 mg/kg; Alexion stopped development.
efficacy.quote: there was no clear evidence overall of clinically meaningful improvement in neurocognitive function at the higher doses investigated
efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint was safety; efficacy scored on the neurocognitive secondary (endpoint_role null). The mouse abstract's CNS claim is taken as a disease-modification prediction.

efficacy.confidence_note: Dog abstract-level; Muschol full text read.
efficacy.model: MPS IIIB dog, ICV tralesinidase alfa (20 months)
efficacy.note: Dogs kept cognition; in patients the DQ co-primary result is not reported and the phase 3 (NCT07579910) has not started.
efficacy.quote: TA-treated MPS IIIB dogs performed better on cognitive tests and had improved CNS pathology and decreased cerebellar volume loss relative to vehicle-treated MPS IIIB dogs.
efficacy.judgement: Muschol 2023 reports correlations of AEq change with exposure and CGMV but not the registered DQ pre/post comparison; sponsor releases of cognitive stabilization (2025-26) are tier 5 and not a primary-endpoint result. Kept untested. Dated 2023 (patient paper) with model_first_use_year 2016 proxy.

patient_trials.quote: Significant correlations were also established between the change in cognitive AEq score and plasma drug exposure, plasma HS-NRE levels, and CGMV.

efficacy.note: Treated Naglu-/- mice behaved normally and lost most storage vacuolation, though improvement was partial in some animals.
efficacy.quote: These results indicate that NaGlu delivery from intracerebral sources has the capacity to alleviate most disease manifestations in the MPSIIIB mouse model.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the mouse predicts that intracerebral NAGLU expression prevents neurological disease.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: developmental quotient decline vs natural history
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; uncontrolled n=4 against natural history; registered primary was safety. Quote from the draft's verified Tardieu 2017 entry.
efficacy.note: All four children still declined but less than natural history at 30 months; youngest near normal.
efficacy.quote: Compared with the natural history of mucopolysaccharidosis type III syndromes, neurocognitive progression was improved in all patients, with the youngest patient having function close to that in healthy children.
efficacy.judgement: Scored on the neurocognitive secondary as the draft does for the dog track (only efficacy readout); partial because decline slowed rather than stopped.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: brain atrophy and neurocognition vs untreated Sanfilippo A/B children at 5.5 years
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC 34405688); n=4, uncontrolled; efficacy was the secondary endpoint; the youngest patient did better than untreated children.
efficacy.note: At 5.5 years, 3 of 4 children had brain atrophy and neurocognition no different from untreated Sanfilippo children despite persistent CSF NAGLU.
efficacy.short: No benefit in 3 of 4 at 5.5 y
efficacy.quote: Patients 2, 3, and 4 showed progressive brain atrophy and neurocognitive evolution that did not differ from untreated Sanfilippo A/B children.
efficacy.reason: Benefit not sustained in older children
efficacy.judgement: Long-term follow-up of the same trial overturns the 30-month signal in 3 of 4 patients, so the mouse prediction of alleviating most disease manifestations is contradicted; the youngest patient's milder course keeps confidence low. The checker flagged the same datum for the dog track.

safety.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
safety.note: Dogs needed immunosuppression to avoid neuroinflammation and loss of transduced cells.
safety.quote: As shown previously in dogs with the closely related Hurler syndrome, immunosuppression was necessary to prevent neuroinflammation and elimination of transduced cells.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; the prediction led the trial to include immunosuppression.

safety.model: MPS IIIB dog, intracerebral rAAV5-hNAGLU with immunosuppression
safety.note: Under immunosuppression, children mounted anti-NAGLU T-cell responses that later subsided; no unexpected serious reactions.
safety.quote: The initial specific anti-NAGLU immune response that later subsided suggested acquired immunological tolerance.
safety.judgement: Paired: dog predicted transgene immunity requiring immunosuppression; patients on immunosuppression showed NAGLU-specific T cells without neuroinflammation (Gougeon 2021). Partial because the untreated-dog outcome (neuroinflammation) could not be tested in patients.

safety.model: Juvenile cynomolgus monkey ICV toxicology (tralesinidase alfa)
safety.note: Juvenile NHP ICV study: drug-related findings limited to CSF and catheter-track cell infiltrates without functional change.
safety.quote: The drug-related changes observed were limited to increased cell infiltrates in the CSF and along the ICV catheter track after ICV administration.
safety.judgement: Opening year 2016 is a proxy (IND-enabling study before the April 2016 trial start); published 2023.

safety.magnitude_basis: CSF inflammatory cell response after ICV dosing
safety.confidence_note: Patient side full text (PMC9843052); NHP abstract-level.
safety.model: Juvenile cynomolgus monkey ICV toxicology (tralesinidase alfa)
safety.note: Patients had drug-related CSF pleocytosis SAEs and device infections, matching NHP CSF/catheter infiltrates but more severe.
safety.short: CSF pleocytosis seen, as in NHP
safety.quote: SAEs assessed by investigators to be related to the study drug were CSF pleocytosis, vomiting, angioedema, fluctuating consciousness, and pyrexia.
safety.judgement: Same harm type, but NHP called it non-functional while patients had SAEs, so partial. Hypersensitivity (8 events) not counted as a miss: NHP response to a human protein is not taken as predictive. Not a retrodiction (study ran pre-IND).
